MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 22, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:03 p.m., on November 22, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 17, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:35 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

RECESS

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury declared recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m.
with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Ury

City Council Minutes  1  November 22, 2016
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 13 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of November 8, 2016, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated October 28, 2016 in the Amount of $1,614,865.36

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated November 4, 2016 in the Amount of $468,530.74

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2016

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2016

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  2  November 22, 2016
 7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  September 2016

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for September 2016

  Received and filed.

9.  City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2015-16 and Annual Review of City
  Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the accompanying City Treasurer's Annual Report for fiscal year
  2015-2016; (2) adopted Resolution 16-52 Approving the City's Investment Policy for FY
  2016-17; and (3) set the Benchmark Index for FY 2016-17 to be a Government Securities
  Index comprised of 60% three-month Treasury Bills; 25% Treasury and Agency securities
  with maturities greater than one year and up to three years; and 15% Treasury and Agency
  securities with maturities greater than three years and up to five years.

10.  Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer’s Annual Report
  for Fiscal Year 2015-16 and Annual Review of the CDFA Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the accompanying Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2015-
  16; and (2) adopted CDFA Resolution 16-03 Approving the Authority's Investment Policy
  for FY 2016-17.

11.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2015-16
  and Annual Review of the Mission Viejo Housing Authority Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the accompanying Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2015-
  16; and (2) adopted Housing Authority Resolution 16-02 Approving the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority Investment Policy for FY 2016-17.

12.  Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule and Authorized Position
  Schedule

  (1) Adopted Resolution 16-53 Amending the City's Salary Schedule and Establishing
  Salary Ranges for Authorized Job Classifications Effective November 19, 2016; and (2)
  adopted Resolution 16-54 Amending the City's Salary Schedule Effective January 1, 2017;
  and (3) adopted Resolution 16-55 Amending the City's Authorized Position Schedule for
  Fiscal Year 2016- 2017.

City Council Minutes  3  November 22, 2016
 Note: Public Comments were taken out of order

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Isaac Rastagar, M.V.: stated that it is very dark at night outside of La Paws dog park and he
suggested that the City install some street lights.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

13.  Library Holiday Schedule for 2017 Calendar Year

  Council Member Schlicht said that when the library was first opened, it was supposed to
  provide a better library system with longer days and less holidays. She stated that the
  Orange County Library is only closed 10 days in 2017 and she is opposed to the three
  additional days that the Mission Viejo Library will be closed.

  Council Member Sachs noted that City employees have had ten paid holidays since 1992.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve proposed
  Library Holiday and Closure Schedule for 2017.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

STAFF REPORTS

22.  Update on “Year of Technology” Projects

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander presented a brief staff report.

  Greg Curtin, CEO of Civic Resource Group: discussed technology projects completed this
  year including the City's Strategic Plan Update, the network infrastructure and server
  update, network assessments, approval and order of a new firewall, and the update of the
  Mission Viejo Website. Mr. Curtin also provided a demonstration of the City's new mobile
  phone app.

NEW BUSINESS

14.  Community Services Funding - Fiscal Year 2016-2017

  Management Analyst Leslie Rea-McDonald presented the staff report and answered the
  City Council Members questions.
City Council Minutes  4  November 22, 2016
   City Attorney Curley recommended that Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum and Council Member
  Raths not vote on funding for organizations that they are involved with and that they leave
  the room during the vote.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
  Community Services Commission’s recommended funding amounts for the Community
  Services Funding Program, fiscal year 2016-17, for all organizations except Crime
  Survivors and Patriots and Paws.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum left the room.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
  Community Services Commission’s recommended funding amount for Crime Survivors.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum returned and Council Member Raths left the room.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
  Community Services Commission’s recommended funding amount for Patriots and Paws.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Sachs, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Raths

  Council Member Raths returned to the room.

15.  Interim Zoning Ordinance, Adopted as an Urgency Measure, Establishing a
  Temporary Moratorium on the Approval of Permits for Uses Involving Directly or
  Indirectly, the Collective Transport of Groups of People and Associated Group
  Assembly in the City and Adopting Findings of Urgency

City Council Minutes  5  November 22, 2016
   City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Craig Foster, M.V.: speaking on behalf of 449 Group, he expressed opposition to the
  proposed ordinance and temporary moratorium.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to (1)
  adopt Interim Zoning Ordinance 16-321, as an Urgency Measure, pursuant to Government
  Code Section 65858, Establishing a Temporary Moratorium on the Approval of Permits
  for Uses Involving, Directly or Indirectly, the Collective Transport of Groups of People
  and Associated Group Assembly in the City; and (2) direct staff to study and explore
  appropriate regulatory options and return with a recommendation to City Council regarding
  the structuring of zoning over a new use/facility and the expansion of an existing
  use/facility involving, directly or indirectly, the collective transport of groups of people
  and associated group assembly.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Note: Item P1 was taken out of order

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Ury presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Miranda A. Bell and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant
  Gregoris E. Nunez.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

16.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA)

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

17.  Foothill/Eastern & San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agencies Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

18.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

City Council Minutes  6  November 22, 2016
 19.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum presented the report.

20.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum presented the report.

21.  Update On CUSD Bond Measure Issue

  Mayor Ury stated that with the failure of Measure M in the recent election, the School
  Board may wish to present a financial proposal that is a little more palatable to the voters.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

23.  Adjustment of Commercial Solid Waste, Food Waste/Organics, and Recycling Rates
  as a Result of State Law Mandating Organics Recycling

  Environmental Program Administrator Denise Matson presented the staff report and
  answered the City Council Member’s questions.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to adopt Resolution 16-
  56 Establishing Rates for a Commercial Food Waste/Organics Service, Establishing Rates
  for Commercial Single-Stream Recycling, and Adjusting Commercial Trash Rates for Bin
  Service by 5.1% Effective January 1, 2017.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

24.  City Update on Status of City and Regional Recreational Drone Regulation: Follow-
  Up to 206 Civil Grand Jury Survey; Report to Civil Grand Jury

  City Attorney Curley presented the report and answered questions of the City Council
  Members.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Ury, to receive the report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  7  November 22, 2016
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

25.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that he met with some concerned citizens last week who believe
that there is a conspiracy or hidden agenda and that the City is going to build a bunch of apartments
across the street from the Civic Center. He stated that during development of the 2015-17 budget,
the Council’s number one priority was economic development. Council Member Raths noted that
he and Council Member Sachs were appointed to an economic development ad hoc committee and
they have studied the civic core issue, hired the Kosmont firm as a consultant and SWA Group to
conduct a vision plan for the civic core. Council Member Raths said that he told this group of
residents that there is no hidden agenda, no apartments, and that the City is simply looking to
upgrade some of the shopping centers along Marguerite and Oso and he wanted to go on record to
debunk the myth.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that the visioning consultant conducted the third and final
meeting last week with about 100 residents in attendance. There were three separate and distinct
plans, one dealing with the Oso Creek, another dealing with new frontage on properties with some
added retail opportunities, and the third idea was a full-blown rehabilitation plan. He said that
about half of the participants wanted to jump immediately to stage three but the basic questions
that the City asked the consultants to address with residents is whether or not the community wants
any changes in the civic core area. Council Member Sachs noted that the overwhelming response
at all of the public meetings was yes, the community has an interest in doing something to improve
the area. He said that he is looking forward to seeing the SWA Group’s final report which will be
presented to the Planning and Transportation Commission in December and to the City Council in
January. Council Member Sachs pointed out that municipalities in California need to pay attention
to the CalPERS Board’s action at its January 2017 meeting. They are getting closer and closer to
making a decision to lower the discount rate from 7.25% to about 80 basis points and that it will
affect every municipality in the state. Council Member Sachs stated that CalPERS can no longer
continue at 7.25% growth rate expectancy when last year the rate was 0.01% and the coming
change will have a tumultuous effect, potentially causing some cities to look at bankruptcy. He
noted that Mission Viejo is fortunate to be very well poised to absorb a rate change with solid
reserves for contingencies but the Council and staff do need to keep an eye on it and be prepared.

City Council Minutes  8  November 22, 2016
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht said that years ago she raised concern about the need for pedestrian
safety enhancements at the lake, including a bridge, and that plans are still in the working
stages. She feels that the City needs to move quicker on the concerns that she has raised about
trees blocking the traffic signals on Muirlands at Marathon and Robin Circle. She said that she is
especially concerned because the ruling in the Cordova vs. City of Los Angeles lawsuit said that
cities can be held liable for its trees when there is an accident and she asked that the trees on
Muirlands at least be trimmed. Council Member Schlicht gave a shout out to the Mission Viejo
High School Diablos football team. She said they have shown good sportsmanship, provided great
memories and they made a huge effort and played 39 games without a loss, showing everyone the
value of teamwork. She noted that the Diablos didn't have a good night last Friday but the
community is already looking forward to next season and she congratulated them on a great run.
Council Member Schlicht said she has congratulated Trish Kelley and Brian Goodell on their
election to the City Council and she said she wishes them nothing but success in serving the
residents. She thanked the residents who voted for her and gave her the opportunity to serve for
eight years. Being on the Council was a great experience and a wonderful privilege and Council
Member Schlicht stated that she has always remained true to the voter and was never afraid to ask
the questions, even though she didn’t get answers. She said that her time on the Council will
always be a cherished memory and she is forever grateful that residents gave her the opportunity
to serve them. In closing, Council Member Schlicht said that the November 8 vote has given her
a four-year start on a new adventure and she shared a quote from Benjamin Franklin: "It is the
responsibility of every citizen to question authority."

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum expressed her kudos to the Diablos football team for a well-fought
season and a long winning streak. Watching them play has been a passion of hers for many years
and she said it was sad for all when they lost last week. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum announced that
the Capistrano Valley High School Cougars football team won in their division and are moving on
to the next round of CIF, the Trabuco Hills High School marching band won in their division in
the Western State Band Tournament, and the Mission Viejo High School band won first place. She
expressed her appreciation for all of the different talents that Mission Viejo students share with
the community. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum mentioned that she would like to have a Neighborhood
Watch Town Hall Meeting in December because this is the season when things happen and it
would be an opportune time to update the community on crime prevention and a good chance for
people to hear about neighborhood watch opportunities. She encouraged residents to also look at
service on a City Commission and to find details and an application form on the City’s
website. She reminded residents of the Santa's arrival and town lighting celebration which is fun
for all ages and a great way to kick off the holidays. The event will be held on Sunday,
November 27, beginning at 3:00 p.m. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum concluded her comments by
expressing her appreciation to staff and her Council colleagues and she wished everyone in the
City a very happy Thanksgiving.

City Council Minutes  9  November 22, 2016
 Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury reminded residents to arrive early for the Santa's arrival celebration and to consider
parking across the street as it will be very busy.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:08 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, December 13, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of December 13, 2016

City Council Minutes  10  November 22, 2016
